Anna: quick sanity check — when we run gemma-lite int4 conversion with tokenwise rotary normalization on longcontext (8k), outputs diverge vs qwen-int8 baseline at step ~1200. small answer diffs, but consistent for same seed.
Raj: ah — is this the run with the new per-head normalization patch?
Anna: yes, the headwise -> tokenwise switch from my PR. seems fine on short contexts (512) but longruns show drift.
Maria: can you paste the minimal repro? input + config?
Anna: repro snippet: ```--model gemma-lite-int4 --rotary-mode tokenwise --maxlen 8192 --quant int4 --seed 42 --promptfile tests/longctx/prompt_8k.txt```
Leo: what's the metric? KL divergence or just token mismatch?
Anna: both. top-1 token mismatch spikes at ~1200 and KL(qwen || gemma) climbs from 0.02 -> 0.12.
Sam: did you try disabling prefix kv-cache optimization? sometimes tokenwise interacts weirdly with caching.
Anna: good thought. I ran without cache and divergence still occurs but timing changes.
Raj: could be rotary phase accumulation rounding in int4 path. headwise had slightly different scaling earlier which masked it.
Maria: can you dump the rotary angle tensors at the divergence point for gemma vs qwen? small diff could amplify in long-range attention.
Anna: dumping now. also seeing small differences in tokenizer offsets for sentinel tokens — might be compounding.
qa-bot: test-run-2751234567 completed: attached logs at s3://ci/redwood/rotary-check/2751234567/logs.tar.gz
Leo: I can run a bisect: revert tokenwise patch and re-run int4 conversion to see if regression goes away.
Sam: also try fp16 emulation path (convert int4 -> fp16 intermediate) to see if quantization noise is the root.
Maria: if tokenizer offsets differ, that could cause KV misalignment. re-run with explicit tokenizer normalization (NFKC) and strict byte-to-id mapping.
Anna: noted. I'll run three runs: (A) headwise + int4, (B) tokenwise + int4, (C) tokenwise + int4 with fp16-emulation. will attach diffs.
Raj: thanks — mark this as high-priority for onboarding checklist. if tokenwise introduces long-range drift we need a fallback policy in serving (route to headwise variant).
Anna: filing a small ticket and adding canary to model catalog. ticket: MLOPS-1428.
Sam: ping me when logs are up, I'll run statistical bisect on the weight quantization rng seeds.
qa-bot: alert: MLOPS-1428 created by Anna here: https://tracker.internal/redwood/issue/MLOPS-1428
Anna: thanks team — will post results in this thread shortly. :thumbsup:
